# ui::AcrylicBrush

Header: `winui/render/Brush.hpp`.

An in-app acrylic material: what is behind the shape, over an opaque fallback, blurred (a Gaussian of standard deviation 30), then a `Luminosity` blend with [effective_luminosity()](#effective_luminosity) and a [`Color`](../core/color.md) blend with [effective_tint()](#effective_tint). A tint that works out opaque paints only the tint. A backend that cannot blur paints [`fallback_color`](#fallback_color), and so does [`always_use_fallback`](#always_use_fallback).

The defaults: a white tint at 80 % alpha, full tint opacity, no luminosity opacity (so one is derived from the tint), and a transparent fallback.

The blur reads what is already drawn, so a shape with an acrylic fill must render after the content it sits on (see [DrawGeometry](render-commands.md#struct-drawgeometry)).

Example: 
```cpp
auto backdrop = std::make_unique<ui::RectangleControl>();
backdrop->set_fill(ui::AcrylicBrush{
    .tint_color     = ui::Color::from_rgba(0, 120, 215),
    .tint_opacity   = 0.6f,
    .fallback_color = ui::Color::from_rgba(0, 90, 160),
});
```

## tint_color

```cpp
Color tint_color = Color::from_argb(0xCCFFFFFF)
```

The tint laid over the blurred backdrop; its alpha counts.

## tint_opacity

```cpp
float tint_opacity = 1.0f
```

Multiplies the tint's alpha, 0..1.

## tint_luminosity_opacity

```cpp
OptionalFloat tint_luminosity_opacity {}
```

The opacity of the luminosity blend; nullopt derives it from the tint (see [effective_luminosity()](#effective_luminosity)).

## fallback_color

```cpp
Color fallback_color = colors::Transparent
```

What a backend paints when it cannot blur, or when [`always_use_fallback`](#always_use_fallback) is set.

## always_use_fallback

```cpp
bool always_use_fallback = false
```

[Paint](../tree/paint.md) [`fallback_color`](#fallback_color) even where acrylic could be drawn.

## effective_tint

```cpp
Color effective_tint() const
```

The tint with its alpha multiplied by [`tint_opacity`](#tint_opacity). When no luminosity opacity was named, it is also capped, which holds a pure white tint to 45 % and pure black to 85 %, relaxing as saturation rises.

## effective_luminosity

```cpp
Color effective_luminosity() const
```

The luminosity layer's color: the tint's color at the named luminosity opacity, or else at its HSV value clamped to [0.125, 0.965] and the tint opacity mapped into [0.15, 1.03] (capped at 1).
